newsitem.title: USA: "Big Dig" to double Boston crossing tolls - report.
newsitem.headline: "Big Dig" to double Boston crossing tolls - report.

text.p: The Massachusetts Turnpike Authority (MassPike) and the Massachusetts Port Authority (MassPort) are likely to double tolls on Boston Harbor crossings to help pay for the Third Harbor/Central Artery Project construction, according to a report in Wednesday's Boston Herald.

The newspaper, citing unnamed sources, said the doubling of tolls on the Tobin Bridge, operated by MassPort, and the Sumner-Callahan and Ted Williams Tunnels, run by MassPike, could be among the funding solutions in a long-awaited state study slated for release next week.
A state legislative ban on passenger vehicle toll increase for both the bridge and the tunnels expires on Sunday.

The project, popularly known at the "Big Dig" is estimated to cost at least $10.7 billion with the federal government picking up 85 percent of the costs. Massachusetts must come up with a way of funding its share, estimated to be between $3.0 and $3.6 billion.
Neither MassPort nor MassPike officials could be immediately reached for comment.
